audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 2 and 3 were given to Rumble although whys[1] and whys[2] say Kennen wins the ranged trade and owns the poke war; Level 6 was 'Skill' and first item was Rumble although whys[4] and whys[5] say the stun-lock blows him up and the first item cashes it into a kill.
audit.why: 52.54% over 177 games: Kennen out-ranges Flamespitter's 600 cone for the whole early game and holds the ult window, and only the scaling AP bruiser stage past two items belongs to Rumble. The packet chart matches.
audit.corrected: L1 Skill, L2 Kennen, L3 Kennen, Levels 4-5 Skill, L6 Kennen, first item Kennen, 2+ items Rumble.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game flip is described without the ult cooldowns that drive it.
audit.why: Mirror finding reused: Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120s at every rank while The Equalizer is 130/105/80. Kennen holds the ult edge at rank 1 and loses it entirely by Rumble's rank 3, which is exactly when the two-item row turns.
audit.corrected: whys[6] now states the 80s versus 120s comparison.

audit.whatIsWrong: Electro Harpoon is described only as a slow. It also reduces magic resist and he carries two charges — which matters on a page whose headline advice is 'Build MR'. Flamespitter is also treated as a burst rather than a 3-second cone he walks with.
audit.why: Riot text: E Electro Harpoon, 850 range, two stored charges, slows and reduces Magic Resist, stronger in Danger Zone; Q Flamespitter, 600 range, 10/9/8/7/6s, damage in a cone for 3 seconds. Mirror finding: the trade window is the cone's duration, not a cast time.
audit.corrected: Both harpoons shred your MR before the cone lands, and Flamespitter burns for 3 seconds while he walks — leave the cone, do not try to out-trade inside it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Scrap Shield is presented as the matchup-defining cooldown to track before every engage. It is a flat 6 seconds — it is back for essentially every trade, so it cannot be the window you plan around.
audit.why: Rumble kit: W Scrap Shield, flat 6s. The cooldowns that actually gate his power are the heat bar and The Equalizer at 130/105/80s.
audit.corrected: Say the shield is 6s and point the tracking at his heat bar and his ult instead.

audit.why: packet flagged 'His Equalizer' as a probable wrong name; The Equalizer is the correct Riot name and the distance is only the possessive replacing the article. False positive, no edit.

edits.before: - Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining — Bait it, then commit. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Rumble Scrap Shield: a flat 6s, so it is back every trade — track his heat bar and The Equalizer (130s) instead. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: Bait it, then commit. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: It is only 6s — bait it, then commit inside that same trade.

edits.before: He can reach Danger Zone heat and an E-harpoon can stick you in the cone, so respect his overheat trades and only poke.
edits.after: Danger Zone heat plus two harpoons that slow and shred your MR can stick you in the cone, so respect it and only poke.

edits.before: His Equalizer zones you off objectives and his overheated Flamespitter out-DPSes your squishy body once your R is down.
edits.after: The Equalizer falls to 80s against your flat 120, so he zones every objective while Flamespitter out-DPSes your body.

edits.before: Land the E harpoon slow to stick you inside Flamespitter for sustained burn DPS
edits.after: Land both harpoons to shred your MR and hold you in a 3-second Flamespitter cone

notes: Mirror (rumble__kennen) was already audited and its two findings were reused rather than re-derived. That mirror also reported a systemic template defect in champ-data/rumble.full.js — dosFull/dontsFull titles paired with generic descriptions that do not match them. The same defect exists on this page: dontsFull[1] 'Stand in his R line' carries 'Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown', and dontsFull[2] 'Fight in his flamespitter' carries the generic E-burn description. I did not rewrite them here because it is a champion-wide template issue rather than a Rumble-specific fact, and it affects every matchup page equally.
